// diagnostic

E2307

A declared string view would outlive a possible owning `String`, has no stable public owner set, or `copies: .Explicit` forbids the owning materialization needed at a non-view destination.

What

A declared string view would outlive a possible owning `String`, has no stable public owner set, or `copies: .Explicit` forbids the owning materialization needed at a non-view destination.

Why

`View<str>` follows the same inferred owner-set rule as `View<T>` through calls, aggregates, callbacks, and trait contracts. Local and temporary owners still die too soon; an owned `String` still cannot fill a declared `View<str>` slot.

Fix

Keep every possible owner alive, use a proven `View<str>` boundary, write `~view` at an explicit-copy boundary, or remove `copies: .Explicit` for the default owning copy.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E2307: tests/ui/owned_string_as_view_str.stderr.

Error [E2307]: an owned `String` cannot fill a `View<str>` slot
  --> tests/ui/owned_string_as_view_str.jet:7:29
    |
  7 |     return TitleView{value: title}
    |                             ^^^^^
 Why: `View<str>` needs a zero-copy window from `.trim()` / `.after()` / `.before()` (or an already-tracked string-view binding); a plain `String` place owns its buffer instead
 Fix: bind a window with `.trim()`/`.after()`/`.before()`, return a `View` of the owning element and read the field through it, or store an owned `String` field and copy with `~`
